about: The epistle of the Fourth Sunday of Advent. Paul takes the verdict away from the Corinthians and from himself alike — it belongs to the Lord, and it is not given until He comes.

seg.tr: Brethren: Let each one regard us thus, as ministers of Christ and dispensers of the mysteries of God.
Here, now, it is required among the dispensers that one be found faithful.
But to me it is of the least account that I be judged by you or by man’s day; but neither do I judge myself.

ex.w033: Paul speaks of a human day of judgment, that is, a human tribunal.

seg.tr: For I am not conscious of anything against myself, yet this does not justify me; the Lord is the One who judges me.

a.g: For I am conscious of nothing against myself

seg.tr: Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes. He will bring to light the things hidden in darkness and reveal the counsels of hearts; then each will receive praise from God.
